string-array.name: sentences_cbt
string-array.item: A thought is a thought, not a fact. I can check it before I believe it.
What is the evidence for this thought, and what is the evidence against it?
What would I tell a good friend who had this thought?
Small steps first: doing a little changes how I feel more than waiting does.
Feelings rise and fall like waves. This one will pass.
Is there another way to see this? Try one more.
I notice the worry, I name it, and I choose my next small action.
Not “always” and not “never”: what really happened today?

string-array.name: sentences_cogfun
string-array.item: A plan on paper frees my mind to do the task.
One task at a time. What is the very first step?
Set a timer and let it keep the time for me.
Prepare tonight what I will need tomorrow.
Break it into pieces I can finish in five minutes.
Put it where I will see it: reminders belong in sight.
Check: what do I need, in what order, and how long will it take?
Routines save energy. Each repeat gets a little easier.

string-array.name: sentences_nlp
string-array.item: Start with the outcome: what do I want, and how will I know I have it?
The map is not the territory: another point of view is always possible.
Same situation, new frame: what else could this mean?
Picture it going well, in colour, step by step, and feel it.
Choose the words I use on myself. Words steer attention.
Anchor a good moment: remember it, and press thumb and finger together.
Ask better questions: “How can I?” opens more doors than “Why can’t I?”
I can step into someone else’s shoes for a minute, then back into mine.

string-array.name: sentences_adhd
string-array.item: My brain works differently, not worse. I can build supports that fit it.
Start with two minutes. Starting is the hardest part.
Move a little, then focus: the body helps the mind.
Make it visible: a timer, a list, a note where my eyes go.
Celebrate finishing, even the small things.
If I drift, I just gently come back. No blame.
One thing at a time, with a short break after.
A reward right now helps the brain keep going: choose a small one.

string-array.name: sentences_anxiety
string-array.item: Breathe in for four, out for six. Slow breaths tell the body it is safe.
Name five things I can see. I am here, now.
Worry is a guess about the future, not a fact.
I can feel afraid and still take one small step.
Put the worry in a box for now; I can open it later.
My body is safe right now. Feel my feet on the floor.
What is the kindest thing I can do for myself this minute?
This feeling is uncomfortable, not dangerous. It will pass.

string-array.name: sentences_organize
string-array.item: A place for everything makes mornings calm.
Gear by the door tonight means no searching tomorrow.
If it takes two minutes, do it now.
A short list beats a long one. Pick the top three.
Same time, same order: habits do the organising for me.
Plan a buffer: leave a little extra time for the unexpected.
Done is better than perfect. Tick it off.
Clear one small surface and feel the difference.

string-array.name: sentences_motivation
string-array.item: I do not wait for motivation. I start, and motivation follows.
Every finished routine is a vote for the person I want to be.
Look at how far I have come, not only how far there is to go.
Small steps every day beat a big plan once.
I can do hard things, one step at a time.
A mistake is a step in learning. I try again.
Reward the effort, not only the result.
Today I choose one thing I am proud to do.
